title: The Latest in U.S.-China AI Competition | Council on Foreign Relations
gist: A CFR interview with senior fellow Chris McGuire argues that Moonshot AI's newly open-weighted Kimi K3 proves China is holding a steady 6-8 month lag behind U.S. frontier models only by leaning harder on U.S. chips, U.S. cloud, and distillation of U.S. models — which makes compute cutoffs, not open-weight bans, the effective lever. McGuire calls for Commerce ICTS rules and export controls that bar Chinese models from U.S. businesses, U.S. cloud, and U.S. AI chips worldwide, and predicts the U.S. lead expands over the next year even as a damaging AI-driven cyber incident becomes likely.

insights.claim: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, released July 16 2026 with weights posted publicly, is likely the most capable Chinese model and the best open-weight model, but a joint U.S.-UK government assessment places it roughly six months behind U.S. models in cyber capabilities despite Moonshot's claim of parity with top U.S. models.

insights.claim: A workable ban on Chinese AI models would run through three Commerce Department levers — ICTS regulations barring businesses from transacting with Chinese AI companies via their APIs, ICTS regulations barring U.S. cloud providers from hosting and serving those models, and export controls prohibiting U.S. AI chips anywhere in the world from being used to run them — applying to all Chinese models open- or closed-weight while exempting U.S. open-weight models and stopping short of criminalizing individual downloads.
